turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please come in, Mrs. Iyer, and sit comfortably. I have a short while before my next patient, so we can go through this without rushing.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I am sorry to trouble you. My daughter has accompanied me, as she looks after my tablets.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Good morning, doctor. I am Meena. I live with Amma, and every Sunday I fill her pill box.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): That helps me a great deal. Mrs. Iyer, what has been troubling you?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, both my ankles have swollen, and I become a little short of breath when I walk.
[SEG0006] person_3 (CAREGIVER): By evening the slippers do not go on, doctor. In the morning the swelling is somewhat less, but it is still there.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has this swelling been present?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): About two weeks, doctor. Before that, my feet were quite normal.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the breathlessness, did it begin around then as well?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor, the same two weeks. It is only slight, and only while walking.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does the breathlessness come on when you are resting, or when you lie flat at night?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. Sitting or lying down, I am comfortable only. I still use just one pillow.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain with the walking?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain, doctor. None whatsoever.
[SEG0015] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She has not had any fever either. Her meals are as usual, though she says the feet feel heavy.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm. Swelling for two weeks, heavy feet, breathless only on walking. Before I examine you, let us sort the tablets, because the list can mislead us.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): In the morning she has the little white one for BP, and the water tablet. At night, the cholesterol tablet.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Can you name the little white one, and the strength?
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It is amlodipine 5 mg, one tablet in the morning, by mouth. I checked the strip yesterday.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I have had high blood pressure for fifteen years, doctor. I have taken that tablet for a long time.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Understood. Now, the phrase water tablet can mean more than one drug. Which medicine is it, exactly?
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Furosemide, 40 mg, one in the morning, by mouth, for the swelling. She was already on it before this recent worsening.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I take Lasix also, doctor. The previous physician had written Lasix on the old prescription.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ah, there it is, the same tablet counted twice. Lasix is the water tablet itself, only the brand name of furosemide. It is not an extra medicine.

[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Oh, I see. I had written both names in my diary, so I thought they were two. In the box, though, I put only one 40 mg tablet each morning. I never give a second one at night.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then we record it once: furosemide 40 mg every morning by mouth. Please do not add another dose because the ankles are puffy.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly, doctor. I will not take anything beyond what you advise.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the night tablet for cholesterol, what is the name, and what dose is printed?
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Atorvastatin, one capsule, sorry, one tablet, at night, by mouth. The dose, um, I think maybe 20 mg. I threw away the old strip, so I am not fully sure.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will put it down as possibly 20 mg, and I am leaving that medicine unchanged today. If you find a strip at home, bring it next time.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): There is one more thing, doctor, if you please. A tablet was stopped by another doctor.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, tell me which one.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Dr. Krishnan stopped the ramipril. He told me it was the cause of my cough.
[SEG0034] person_3 (CAREGIVER): That was about six weeks back. After he stopped it, the dry cough settled. She has not swallowed a ramipril since that day.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): So at present, is there any cough at all?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. The cough has gone completely.

[SEG0037] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, may I ask a small thing? My sister takes biotin capsules for her hair fall. They are sitting in our fridge. Should Amma have one daily as well, since it is just a vitamin?
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): No, please don't. That biotin belongs to your sister. Her hair fall is not a reason for your mother to start it.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I quite agree, doctor. I should not take another person's medicine.
[SEG0040] person_3 (CAREGIVER): One practical worry. My husband keeps his metformin on the same kitchen shelf, for his own sugar. I try not to mix the boxes.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep his metformin entirely separate. Your mother is not on metformin, and I am not prescribing it for her.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Please go ahead and examine me, doctor.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me take the observations. Blood pressure is 152 over 88, the pulse is 76 beats per minute, and the oxygen saturation is 97 percent.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that pressure a cause for worry, doctor?

[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): It is mildly up, not an emergency today. On looking, both ankles have pitting oedema up to the lower shin. The chest is clear, with no crackles. Heart sounds are normal, and I do not hear a murmur.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I am relieved the chest is clear. What do you feel is the cause?

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me reason it out. Amlodipine quite often swells the ankles, your lungs are clear, and you are not breathless lying flat. My working impression is that the swelling is due to the amlodipine, not heart failure. I still would not call that final.
[SEG0048] person_3 (CAREGIVER): So will you stop it altogether?

[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am changing that one medicine, not stopping the blood pressure treatment. From tomorrow, amlodipine 2.5 mg, one tablet every morning by mouth, instead of the 5 mg. The smaller dose should be kinder to the ankles.
[SEG0050] person_3 (CAREGIVER): So tomorrow morning I discard the 5 mg and put only the 2.5? Not both?
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Correct, not both. The furosemide stays exactly as it is, 40 mg once every morning. Do not double it.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Very good, doctor. My daughter will set the box accordingly.

[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): I also want a blood test for kidney function, sodium, and potassium, since you take the water tablet. I am sending the form today, and the laboratory can take the sample before you go home.
[SEG0054] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She has had only tea. Must she be fasting?
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): No, fasting is not needed for this test. Tea is perfectly alright only.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): That is kind of you to explain, doctor.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): At home, rest with the legs raised in the afternoon, and keep the salt a little lower in the cooking. No extra water tablet, and no biotin.
[SEG0058] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I already use less salt. I will put a pillow under her calves after lunch.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please come back to see me in two weeks, with the blood report, and with the atorvastatin strip if it turns up.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor, we will come in two weeks.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the swelling becomes suddenly much worse, or if you are breathless even while sitting, do not wait those two weeks, come sooner.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you kindly, doctor. We are grateful for your time.

features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
